query: Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: department_avg_completion
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by quantifying per-department average completion, the exact axis of comparison. Values are derivable by grouping percent_complete by department; row samples show consistent department-level constants, warranting the aggregate.

per_column.name: exceeds_dept_avg
per_column.rationale: A flag for whether a goal beats its department's average gives a useful within-department comparison axis. Values follow soundly from comparing percent_complete to department_avg_completion.

per_column.name: exceeds_overall_avg
per_column.rationale: Complements the dept-relative flag by benchmarking against the global mean, enabling cross-department normalization. Somewhat redundant with exceeds_dept_avg but adds a distinct reference point. Derivable from percent_complete vs. overall mean.

per_column.name: status_numeric
per_column.rationale: A numeric encoding of the existing 'state' field is largely a restatement of an original column, limiting new analytical leverage, though it can aid modeling/correlation with achievement. Values appear to be a straightforward mapping of state, grounded but not confirmable from the text-only samples.

judge.rationale: The added columns center on completion aggregates and relative-performance flags that directly support explaining why achievement rates differ across departments. Values are sound aggregations/comparisons of existing numeric fields with no observed hallucinations; status_numeric is the weakest as it mostly re-encodes an existing column.
